A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WHOOPS-AHA! study, models, and intervention framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on LLaVA-NeXT and Gemma3, including head attribution, interventions, image-patch ablations, and generation-quality analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds dataset validation, MLP interventions, Visual CounterFact evaluation, POPE controls, and quantitative localization results.

M1.justification: Logit Lens head identification, bidirectional attention intervention, and attention/gradient patch selection remain unchanged. V2 reverses the equations' lambda signs to match the steering direction already described and plotted in v1; this does not establish a changed underlying procedure. New controls and localization metrics extend evaluation.

E1.justification: V2 adds Visual CounterFact's color split, covering independently constructed, more photorealistic attribute conflicts, and POPE's object-presence questions for ordinary visual understanding. These substantially extend evaluation beyond WHOOPS-AHA!'s anomalous-scene completions. The original WHOOPS-AHA! coverage remains.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds MLP-block interventions as a comparison with attention-head interventions. Table 4 adds random heads to the localization comparison against gradients. Random heads already appeared in v1's intervention controls, but their participation in this localization comparison is new.

E3.justification: New protocols include interventions on the last three MLP blocks, dataset-specific head identification on Visual CounterFact, a 1,000-question POPE control, and SAM3-mask localization on 20 images. V2 also adds two-model dataset judging and validation by two humans on 20 items. The original models and retained WHOOPS-AHA! sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 tests whether MLP interventions reproduce the effects, whether selected heads support ordinary visual understanding, whether findings replicate across datasets, and whether attention aligns with counterfactual object masks. It also adds dataset-quality validation. V1's random-head control, head-count sensitivity, patch ablations, and generation-quality analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 adds rating summaries with plus/minus values, exact and adjacent agreement rates, localization medians and interquartile ranges, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests against baselines. These substantially expand statistical reporting beyond v1's plotted error bars. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated experimental runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Original WHOOPS-AHA! result curves are retained, while substantial new results appear. Table 3 reports unchanged POPE accuracy of 0.84/0.87 after head suppression, versus 0.50 without images. Table 4 reports localization medians of 4.41/2.05 for counterfactual heads versus 1.74/1.88 for gradients. V2 also adds MLP, dataset-validation, and Visual CounterFact intervention and head-overlap results.

T1.justification: Appendix I introduces the mathematical definition of Average Ratio, comparing mean attribution inside counterfactual object masks with background attribution. This adds a formal metric definition, but no theorem, proof, or substantial theoretical development.

C1.justification: The four headline contributions remain. V2's conclusion additionally asserts that the identified heads are conflict-specific rather than generically visual, strengthening the mechanistic claim. Dataset novelty is also qualified through an explicit combination of requirements rather than the earlier broad first-dataset formulation.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of weak MLP interventions, cross-dataset head overlap, and POPE invariance as evidence of specialized conflict resolution. It adds fusion-architecture generalizability limits while dropping v1's explicit synthetic-data caveat. Appendix E also strengthens diminishing returns after 20 heads into a peak/no-further-gains assertion, although Figure 10 shows continued gains.

D1.justification: V2 adds exact judge model identifiers, OpenRouter usage, judge and human evaluation prompts and rubrics, and Visual CounterFact prompt instructions. Reported total compute changes from 15 to 20 GPU hours. Hardware, Transformers usage, and the code/dataset link are retained; the reproducibility paragraph is relocated.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially expanded and reorganized around multimodal conflicts, VLM interpretability, and internal conflict dynamics. Added discussions include Hua, Basile, Neo, Nikankin, and other works. Positioning now emphasizes implicit commonsense conflicts and conflict-specific heads relative to explicit modality conflicts and general visual processing.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, related work, discussion, and conclusion; separates Dataset from Background and Methods; condenses existing explanations; and reorganizes limitations and appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: V2 adds MLP-intervention and Visual CounterFact plots plus dataset-validation, POPE, and localization tables. It substantially reorganizes appendix displays, relocates existing figures and the caption-generation table, revises captions, and restyles prompt boxes. Original main-result plots are preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 materially strengthens empirical support through independent-dataset replication, MLP/POPE controls, and object-mask localization measurements with significance tests, extending v1's single-dataset study and patch-ablation evidence. Documented dataset validation also improves transparency. These gains outweigh the small validation subsets, overly categorical conflict-specificity interpretation, and new Appendix E assertion that accuracy peaks at 20 heads despite further gains in Figure 10.
